messages:
Maya T: quick check — weekly KPI shows a post-launch spike in 'organic campaign' leads after the launch-post. can analytics confirm this isn't a UTM parsing or GA4 vs server mismatch? :thinking_face:

Jon H: digging in. GA4 event counts are ~30% higher than server-side lead receipts for same window. suspect stray utm_medium values from syndicated partners.

Priya K: we pushed syndication to partner network on 2024-04-02 and some partners append ?utm_medium=partner&utm_campaign=launchX which GA4 maps to 'organic' by our filter rules. Oops.

Lina S: can we get a breakdown by utm_source/utm_medium and then surface a 'clean' KPI line that excludes known syndication sources? want to avoid inflating the exec weekly.

Jon H: yes. I'll create a filtered series and annotate the board. SQL I plan to use:
```sql
SELECT date, COUNT(*) AS ga4_leads, SUM(CASE WHEN utm_source NOT IN ('partnerA','partnerB') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS clean_leads
FROM ga4_events
WHERE event_name='lead' AND date BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2024-04-07'
GROUP BY date;
```

Priya K: also recommend we add a dashboard dimension for 'ingested source' (srv vs ga4) so we can flag future divergences automatically. queueing a ticket.

Maya T: thanks — two asks: 1) add the clean_leads series + annotation on the KPI board; 2) draft a 2-line note for the exec digest clarifying the syndication attribution and corrected numbers.

dashbot: KPI board updated with 'clean_leads' series and annotation "syndication utm mapping caused GA4 spike; cleaned series excludes partner sources". public: https://dash.redwood.com/r/kpi-weekly (annotation id: a-20240402-synd)

Maya T: perfect. once we have the cleaned snapshot post-update, I'll share to #marketing and include the note for execs. :thumbsup:
